title: Dual stalks and contragredient local Frobenius
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Y_0$ be a finite-type $k_0$-scheme, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a lisse finite-rank $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Write $\mathcal F^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\Qlb}(\mathcal F,\Qlb_Y)$ for its linear dual, with the contragredient Weil structure (the inverse Weil isomorphism acts by precomposition), as in [def-real-weil-representation-operations]. Then $\mathcal F^\vee$ is again a lisse finite-rank $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf, in particular a constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf in the sense of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. For every closed point $y\in|Y_0|$ and geometric point $\bar y$ over it, with local geometric Frobenius $F_y$ as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ is finite-dimensional, $F_{y,\mathcal F}$ is an automorphism, and there is a $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$
 c_y:(\mathcal F^\vee)_{\bar y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_{\Qlb}(\mathcal F_{\bar y},\Qlb)
$$
such that, for all $\lambda\in(\mathcal F^\vee)_{\bar y}$ and $v\in\mathcal F_{\bar y}$,
$$
 c_y(F_{y,\mathcal F^\vee}\lambda)(v)=c_y(\lambda)(F_{y,\mathcal F}^{-1}v).
$$
In particular the Frobenius on the dual stalk is conjugate to $(F_{y,\mathcal F}^{-1})^*$.

proof.text: Use [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] for the underlying lisse object of $\mathcal F$. By the finite-stage convention in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], enlarge a finite coefficient field $E$ so that the sheaf, its Weil isomorphism $\theta$, and $\theta^{-1}$ are all represented over $E$ and are inverse there. Work with the resulting finite locally free $E_Y$-module $L$. All tensor, pullback and fibre comparisons below are the normalized comparisons in that realization theorem; at the end extend scalars from $E$ to $\Qlb$. In particular no Frobenius-stable integral lattice is being assumed, and no equivalence with the project's distinct concrete WeilSheaf category is being assumed.

proof.text: Put $L^*=\mathcal Hom_{E_Y}(L,E_Y)$ using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. On a finite-free chart $L=E_Y^r$, a module map $L\to E_Y$ is uniquely $(x_i)\mapsto\sum_i a_ix_i$, so $L^*=E_Y^r$ with coordinate dual basis. The evaluation is $b(\lambda,v)=\lambda(v)$; the local map $E_Y\to L\otimes L^*$ sends $1$ to $\sum_i e_i\otimes e_i^*$. This tensor is independent of basis: after $e'_i=\sum_j e_jP_{ji}$ the dual basis transforms by $P^{-1}$ and the double sum contracts to $\sum_j e_j\otimes e_j^*$. The local coevaluations therefore agree on overlaps and glue by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]. The two triangle identities follow on each chart from $\sum_i e_i^*(v)e_i=v$ and $\sum_i\lambda(e_i)e_i^*=\lambda$, hence hold globally by uniqueness in that gluing statement. This includes $r=0$. Thus $L^*$ is lisse of finite rank. By [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] it defines an object of the constructible heart, and its evaluation and coevaluation are the ones in that coefficient category.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pur-ringed-site-finite-free-dual-pullback] to the geometric-Frobenius pullback $g=g_Y$, the coefficient ring sheaf $E_Y$ on source and target with the ring map $g^{-1}E_Y\to E_Y$ of the realization's pullback, and $L$. Its evaluation-defined comparison identifies $g^*L^*$ with $(g^*L)^*$. Follow it by precomposition with $\theta^{-1}:L\to g^*L$ (and the coefficient-unit identification). This is an isomorphism $\theta^*:g^*L^*\to L^*$, so gives $L^*$ the contragredient Weil structure. In these identifications,
$$b(\theta^*\lambda,\theta v)=\lambda(\theta^{-1}\theta v)=\lambda(v)=g^*b(\lambda,v).$$
This equality of module maps is an equality of Weil morphisms under [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. The same construction identifies the object with the linear dual specified in the item, because locally both are the coordinate dual with this evaluation, and the transition maps on dual bases are inverse transposes. It is therefore a lisse finite-rank constructible Weil sheaf, by step 2 and [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

proof.text:
Fix a closed point $y$ of degree $r$ and its geometric point $x=\bar y$. In [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace] its return is $g_Y^rx=xg_s^r$, not $g_Y^rx=x$. Iterate the evaluation identity in step 3: if it holds for $\theta^{[n]}$, pull back the one-step identity by $g_Y^n$ and compose to obtain it for $\theta^{[n+1]}$; the case $n=1$ is step 3. Pull back by $x$ and evaluate at $s$. Point transport is the restriction-and-coprojection map of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport]. Restriction of a pairing evaluates restrictions of its arguments, and the inverse-image coprojection sends a pure tensor to the tensor of its two images. Thus these maps take $b(\lambda,v)$ to the evaluation of the transported arguments. On the coefficient unit they fix every constant scalar. The composition and point-transport normalization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] identifies this computation with precisely the local operators defined in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. Hence the induced stalk pairing $b_y$ satisfies
$$b_y(F_{y,\mathcal F^\vee}\lambda,F_{y,\mathcal F}v)=b_y(\lambda,v).$$

proof.text:
Write $V=\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ and $D=(\mathcal F^\vee)_{\bar y}$. The functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s Lx^*$ preserves tensor, unit and their constraints by [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization] and [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor], so the two triangle identities of step 2 remain true on $V,D$. Write the image of the coevaluation of $1$ as a finite tensor sum $\sum_jv_j\otimes d_j$. Then $c_y:D\to V^*$, $d\mapsto(v\mapsto b_y(d,v))$, has inverse $\lambda\mapsto\sum_j\lambda(v_j)d_j$: the two composites are identities by those triangle identities. In particular this is the required linear isomorphism. The stalk $V$ is finite-dimensional by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. The local operator is a composite of the iterated Weil isomorphism, pullback-composition isomorphisms and point transports. Point transports are invertible by part 1 of [lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso] (apply that part with the auxiliary separated scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k_0$, so it puts no separatedness assumption on $Y_0$); hence $A=F_{y,\mathcal F}$ is an automorphism. In the identity of step 4 replace $v$ by $A^{-1}v$ to get
$$c_y(F_{y,\mathcal F^\vee}\lambda)(v)=c_y(\lambda)(A^{-1}v).$$
It says exactly $c_yF_{y,\mathcal F^\vee}c_y^{-1}=(A^{-1})^*$. All formulas are compatible with extension from $E$ to $\Qlb$ by the realization theorem, proving the assertions at the stated coefficients.
